## A

gauntlet: gate=gatekeep-pr/final recommended=1

Your PR changes saved recipes to sort by most recent use instead of by title, with a test, so readers can find their recipes quickly. Quick lookup of saved recipes is covered, but the new sort order is not covered because the spec was not updated.

Nothing blocks merging, and every check passed in CI. One smaller point does not block merging: the spec was not updated. The current wording is "Sort saved recipes by title." The proposed wording is "Sort saved recipes by most recent use." The linked ticket asks for most-recent-use order, so the spec should follow the code. Merging without this edit leaves the spec out of date. The fix nits option can make this edit.

You cannot approve your own PR.

I recommend merge because every merge requirement holds.

Pick one:
1. merge - squash-merge the PR with a composed commit message. [recommended]
2. fix nits - make the spec edit, push it, wait for the checks, and come back here.
3. stop - leave the PR open and the checkout as it is.

Type a number; show evidence prints the full record.

## B

One problem blocks merging. The spec says saved recipes sort by title, but the code sorts them by most recent use. For example, "Apple pie" no longer comes before "Zucchini bread" when the bread was opened more recently. The ticket asks only for quick lookup, and sorting by title still gives quick lookup. Keep the title order and change the code to match the spec.

## C

One problem blocks merging. The spec says saved recipes sort by title, but the code sorts them by most recent use. For example, "Apple pie" no longer comes before "Zucchini bread" when the bread was opened more recently. The spec and PR give no reason for the switch beyond changing the order, and the linked ticket could not be read. That leaves no basis for replacing the spec's requirement, so the code needs to return to title order.

## D

One problem blocks merging. A recipe that has never been opened now takes a new code path that no test exercises. The only sort test uses recipes that were opened before, so a mistake in placing an unopened recipe would go unnoticed.

One smaller point does not block merging: the spec was not updated. The current wording is "Sort saved recipes by title." The proposed wording is "Sort saved recipes by most recent use." The ticket asks for this order. Merging without this edit leaves the spec out of date.

## E

1. I map the pick to fix nits and set work_started to true.
2. I save the spec edit's path and its exact old and new wording as the snapshot for this pick, then record the selection as fix-nits.
3. Because no course was set, I start the accounting from the fix-round cap. The entry check passes because a fix-nits selection is still outstanding.
4. I write a findings spec and ledger in the run folder, with a single "fix nits" row.
5. I dispatch a fresh loop-implementer whose working directory is the PR worktree. Its task authorizes only that exact wording change, names a return file, and requires one commit.
6. Admission passes: the tree is clean, there is one commit, and the ledger row is recorded as done.
7. A fresh wave-reviewer checks the range from the pushed head to the local head with this edit as the only authorized change. It reports the edit as resolved, and the push succeeds.
8. I select the scope again at the pushed head. The spec there contains exactly the selected wording and nothing else changed, so the stored scope switches to "Sort saved recipes by most recent use."

## F

Nothing blocks merging. One smaller point does not block merging: the spec was not updated. The spec has no clause about a local trail index. The proposed Design wording is "Keep a local index of trail names so hikers can look them up without a connection." Without this index, looking up a trail needs a network connection, which defeats the offline goal the PR exists for. Merging without this edit leaves the spec out of date.
